cards.explanation: The answer is God Almighty. God tells Moses, Israel's leader, “…as God Almighty, but by My name the LORD I did not make Myself known to them.” (Exodus 6:3) So Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Israel's forefathers, knew Him as God Almighty. Friends, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I can tell you hearing your own name again is a gift.

The answer is foreigners. God calls Canaan “…the land where they lived as foreigners.” (Exodus 6:4) Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Israel's forefathers, lived in the very land God promised to give them. I think that makes the promise feel even bigger.

The answer is groaning. God says, “Furthermore, I have heard the groaning of the Israelites, whom the Egyptians are enslaving…” (Exodus 6:5) He also says He has remembered His covenant. I think it's a comfort that He names the very sound they were making, friends.

The answer is with an outstretched arm and mighty acts of judgment. God says, “I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with mighty acts of judgment.” (Exodus 6:6) Notice who is doing the work. It's God saying "I will," not the Israelites pulling themselves up. Friends, I can't even reach the top shelf without my mustache.

The answer is that He will take them as His own people. God says, “I will take you as My own people, and I will be your God.” (Exodus 6:7) The leaving is only part of it. He is also taking them as His own. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so being wanted means a lot to me.

The answer is True. God says, “And I will bring you into the land that I swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will give it to you as a possession.” (Exodus 6:8) He swore it to the forefathers, and now He says it to their children's children. That's a promise with a long memory.

The answer is False. Moses relayed the message, but “…they did not listen to him.” (Exodus 6:9) Good news was on the table, and it didn't land. I think that tells us something about how heavy their load was.

The answer is their broken spirit and cruel bondage. The verse says it was “…on account of their broken spirit and cruel bondage…” that they did not listen (Exodus 6:9). I think when you're that worn down, even good news is hard to hear. This is a heavy part of the story.

The answer is that if Israel won't listen, why would Pharaoh. Moses says, “If the Israelites will not listen to me, then why would Pharaoh listen to me…” (Exodus 6:12) He's looking at how his own people reacted and doing the math. I bet it felt like a very fair question to him.

The answer is speech. Moses says he is “…unskilled in speech?” (Exodus 6:12) I think he's nervous about talking to Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Friends, I'd be nervous too, because my best speech so far is mumbling through a mustache.

The answer is everything the LORD says to him. God says, “I am the LORD; tell Pharaoh king of Egypt everything I say to you.” (Exodus 6:29) There's no trimming and no leaving out the hard parts. Moses is a messenger, and the whole message goes.

The answer is prophet. God tells Moses, “…your brother Aaron will be your prophet.” (Exodus 7:1) Aaron, Moses' brother, is to tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites go out of his land (Exodus 7:2). Moses had said he was unskilled in speech, and I think a brother at his side must have been welcome news.

The answer is that He will harden it. God tells Moses, “But I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and though I will multiply My signs and wonders in the land of Egypt…” (Exodus 7:3) The text doesn't give a reason here, so we don't add one. It's a heavy line, and we let it stand as written.

The answer is False. Even with His signs and wonders multiplying, God says, “Pharaoh will not listen to you.” (Exodus 7:3-4) Then He says, “…by mighty acts of judgment I will bring the divisions of My people the Israelites out of the land of Egypt.” (Exodus 7:4) So Pharaoh not listening is part of what God tells Moses, and He still says what He will do.

The answer is the Egyptians. God says, “And the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD, when I stretch out My hand against Egypt and bring the Israelites out from among them.” (Exodus 7:5) So it's not only Israel who will know. The people in Egypt will know it too.

The answer is True. “So Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded them.” (Exodus 7:6) Moses had said twice that he was unskilled in speech (Exodus 6:12, 6:30). I bet that wasn't easy, but they did just as He said. Friends, that's an ending I'd frame.

The answer is eighty years old. “Moses was eighty years old and Aaron was eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.” (Exodus 7:7) That's Moses' age at the moment the two of them speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Aaron, his brother, is eighty-three. That's a lot of years behind two men walking in to speak to a king.

The answer is eighty-three. The text says, “Moses was eighty years old and Aaron was eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.” (Exodus 7:7) So Aaron, Moses' brother, is three years older than Moses. Three years apart, and the two of them walk in to speak to Pharaoh together.
